newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- Hotel Industry executives were sorry to see 1996 come to an end because it brought a fourth consecutive year of record profits.
- As bull markets go, the one we're in now has few equals - and it could go on and on.
- Mergers and acquisitions in 1996 soared to more than $647 billion in value, almost three times the 1993 level.

- For decades, few industries have been as cyclical as the automobile business, with sales soaring in good times and and plunging so deeply in bad times that the very survival of some auto makers has been threatened.
- Its residents are nervous, but Hong Kong's economy seems unperturbed by China's impending takeover.

- All floods subside eventually, leaving a mess of mud and rubble. That is Wall Street's fear going into 1997 as analysts fret over whether the great surge of money into equity mutual funds will recede, leaving the market in a shambles.

- As they showed in 1929, economists never displayed much skill in predicting recessions. But historians have found one one thing is common to most periods just before a downturn - the emergence of a wide-spread belief that this time we have found the magic elixir to produce an extended period of prosperity.
